title: CPC 'drought development likely' areas got drought in only 40-43% of their area (CONUS, 2013-2026), and CPC's own precipitation outlooks supported about 35%
abstract: We tested the four classes of the NOAA CPC Seasonal (154 outlooks) and Monthly (159 outlooks) Drought Outlooks against the raw weekly U.S. Drought Monitor at 13,119 CONUS cells for 2013-2026. We wrote the plan before we compared outlooks with outcomes. Development likely areas got D1+ drought in 0.40 (95% year-block interval 0.34-0.46, seasonal) and 0.43 (0.39-0.47, monthly) of their area. Thus the class is not more likely than not. But it has real skill: unflagged no-drought areas developed drought in 0.14 and 0.06. Removal likely verified at 0.71 (0.64-0.77) and 0.56 (0.50-0.61). Remains but improves verified at only 0.36 and 0.41, partly because 36% of seasonal improve area had full removal. CPC's half-category scoring rule cannot see this difference. Development depended on the precipitation outcome: 0.67 and 0.63 with lower-tercile window precipitation, 0.07-0.13 with upper-tercile precipitation. A 0.5 rate needs a lower-tercile chance of about 0.65. In an exploratory check, the CPC precipitation outlooks issued with the drought outlooks gave a mean below-normal probability of only 0.37 and 0.36 in development areas, and equal chances in 57-66% of that area. With these probabilities, the implied development chance is 0.35-0.36, near the observed rates. Thus the 'likely' label claims more than the precipitation information available at issue time. Limitations: CPC gives no number for 'likely'; the USDM is an expert map; area fractions are spatially dependent; the precipitation-outlook part uses a simple tercile conversion and was not pre-registered. Raw source data stay external; the bundle has code, provenance hashes, aggregate tables and three figures.

display.caption: Area fraction with the stated outcome for each CPC drought outlook class, Seasonal (left) and Monthly (right) Drought Outlooks, CONUS 2013-2026. Bars are 95% year-block bootstrap intervals. Diamonds are reference rates: removal in Persists areas and development in unflagged areas that started in D0. The dashed line is 0.5 ('more likely than not').

Development (left) and removal (right) rates against the observed precipitation percentile over the outlook window (1991-2020 base, CPC Unified). Dotted lines: development in unflagged no-drought cells. Vertical lines mark tercile limits.

Left: in development likely areas, CPC's mean below-normal precipitation probability, the observed below-normal share, and the share needed for a 0.5 development rate. Right: observed class rates, rates implied by CPC's precipitation outlooks (with 95% year-block intervals), and rates when the needed tercile occurred. Exploratory analysis.
